result.topic_en: Ramanujan lists his reasons for believing the first Rogers–Ramanujan identity: MacMahon's numerical check, matching asymptotics of both sides as x→1, numerical results from the continued fraction, and the behaviour of the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction at roots of unity.
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94 18 (99)
Rogers-Ram. The
2. The reasons for taking the series
(12) $1+\frac{x}{1-x}+\frac{x^4}{(1-x)(1-x^2)}+\frac{x^9}{(1-x)(1-x^2)(1-x^3)}+\cdots$
$=\frac{1}{(1-x)(1-x^6)(1-x^{11})\cdots}\cdot\frac{1}{(1-x^4)(1-x^9)(1-x^{14})\cdots}$
are the following.
(a). Mr. Macmahon has verified up to $x^{55}$ and found the result correct up to that term.
(b) It can be shewn independently that,
$\log\{\text{L.H.S of (12)}\}\sim\frac{\pi^2}{15(1-x)}$ as $x\to1$
as well as
$\log\{\text{R.H.S of (12)}\}\sim\frac{\pi^2}{15(1-x)}$ as $x\to1$.
(c) The [-numerical-] results of the cont. fraction go to prove the truth of the result.
(d). If $v=\frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^5}{1+}\frac{x^{10}}{1+}\frac{x^{15}}{1+}\cdots$
then $\frac{1}{v}-v-1$ vanishes when $x$ is of the form $e^{i\pi\cdot\frac{m}{n}}$ where $m$ and $n$ are any two integers prime to each other, [-and-] except when $n$ is a multiple of 25.
As a matter of fact, if $v=$ the assumed product of the c.f. $\frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^5}{1+}\frac{x^{10}}{1+}\cdots$

items.english: The reasons for accepting the identity (12) between the series and the product are as follows.

items.quote:

$\log\{\text{L.H.S of (12)}\}\sim\frac{\pi^2}{15(1-x)}$ as $x\to1$
as well as
$\log\{\text{R.H.S of (12)}\}\sim\frac{\pi^2}{15(1-x)}$ as $x\to1$.
items.english: It can be shown independently that the logarithm of each side of (12) is asymptotic to π²/(15(1−x)) as x tends to 1.

items.quote: The [-numerical-] results of the cont. fraction go to prove the truth of the result.
items.english: The results from the continued fraction support the truth of the result.

items.english: Then 1/v − v − 1 vanishes when x = e^{iπm/n} with m, n coprime integers, except when n is a multiple of 25.
